key: a big Mumbai dabbawala network
name: ch00_chess_vs_dabbawala
alt: Split scene: a chess grandmaster thinking hard over one board beside a busy Mumbai station where dabbawalas sort hundreds of tiffins.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel, quiet and spacious: a single elderly chess grandmaster (grey hair, white kurta, reading glasses pushed up on his forehead) sits alone at a small wooden table under one warm hanging lamp, chin resting on his fist, staring intensely at a chessboard with only six pieces left; a large thought bubble above him is filled with branching dotted move-lines, showing deep calculation on very little material. RIGHT panel, crowded and energetic: a wide, slightly elevated view of a Mumbai suburban railway platform at late morning where a dozen dabbawalas in white kurta-pyjamas and white Gandhi caps sort long wooden crates packed with hundreds of round steel tiffins with coloured painted codes on their lids; one lifts a crate onto his head, two others hand tiffins down a human chain into a waiting local train, a cyclist with tiffins hanging from his handlebars rides off, and thin tangled coloured route lines weave between them toward tiny office towers in the background. Each individual action is simple, but there is a huge volume. Soft morning light on both sides; calm on the left, bustling on the right. Labels: "COMPUTE-INTENSIVE" at the top of the left panel, "DATA-INTENSIVE" at the top of the right panel.

key: build a factory kitchen with conveyor
name: ch00_chai_stall_right_size
alt: A tiny roadside chai stall owner refusing an oversized factory kitchen, choosing a small fridge and blender next to his kettle instead.
scene: A wide, eye-level illustration of a narrow Indian street corner in the early evening. In the centre stands a tiny wooden chai stall with a tin roof, a single gas stove, a dented aluminium kettle steaming away, glass tumblers lined up on the counter and a couple of customers sipping chai on a bench. The young owner (mid-20s, rolled-up sleeves, checked lungi, towel over his shoulder) stands beside the stall with a relaxed, satisfied smile. To the LEFT, drawn as a faded, slightly transparent daydream thought cloud rising from him, is a huge gleaming factory kitchen with steel conveyor belts, robotic arms and rows of giant vats, with a large red cross over it and a few banknotes flying away from it. To the RIGHT, solid and real, a small white fridge and a compact countertop blender have just been placed beside the stall, and a customer is happily receiving a tall glass of cold coffee from it, while the kettle keeps serving hot chai. A thin arrow connects the cold-coffee customer to the blender. Warm golden street-light glow, cheerful practical mood. Labels: "PREMATURE OPTIMIZATION" under the crossed-out factory cloud, "RIGHT TOOL" under the fridge and blender.

key: A fault is one fielder dropping a catch
name: ch01_cricket_fault_tolerance
alt: A fielder drops a catch in the slips but a second slip fielder catches the deflection, while a coach runs catching drills on the side.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a sunlit Indian cricket ground during a match. In the centre foreground, behind the batsman and wicketkeeper, a young first-slip fielder in cricket whites and a white sunhat dives and fumbles the ball off his fingertips, a small burst of motion lines showing the drop and a startled expression on his face. Right beside him, a calm second-slip fielder (sturdy build, sunglasses, focused expression) is already reaching out low and cleanly catching the deflected ball, a curved dotted arrow showing the ball's path from the first fielder's hands into his. The bowler in the middle distance raises his arms in celebration. In the lower-right corner, as a small inset circle like a practice-session snapshot, a coach in a tracksuit and cap hits catches with a bat toward three fielders at the nets on purpose, one deliberately mis-hit ball flying high. The scoreboard in the far background is plain and unlabelled. Bright afternoon light, green outfield, lively but composed mood. Labels: "FAULT" next to the fumbling first-slip fielder, "TOLERATED" next to the second-slip catch, "CHAOS DRILL" under the coach inset.

key: notice board vs letterboxes
name: ch01_notice_board_fanout
alt: A housing society lobby with one big notice board on one side and rows of letterboxes being filled with photocopies on the other.
scene: A wide interior view of the ground-floor lobby of an Indian housing society, split visually into two zones. LEFT side: a large cork notice board crowded with dozens of pinned papers of different colours; a tired middle-aged resident in a vest and pyjamas stands close, squinting and running his finger through the clutter to find the one notice he cares about. Posting is cheap: a single person easily pins one more sheet. RIGHT side: a wall of small numbered metal letterboxes in neat rows; the society secretary (elderly man, spectacles, cardigan) feeds a copy of the same notice into each letterbox from a tall stack of photocopies beside a busy photocopier, a fan of thin arrows spreading from his stack into many boxes, while a young woman calmly opens her own letterbox and reads her copy instantly. In the top-left of the board, one large official-looking notice with a municipal seal shape stays only on the board, and the young woman glances over her shoulder at it. Soft overhead tube-light glow mixed with daylight from the entrance, ordinary everyday mood. Labels: "READ ON DEMAND" above the notice board, "FAN-OUT ON WRITE" above the letterboxes, "CELEBRITY" beside the municipal notice.

key: A sweet shop before Diwali
name: ch01_sweet_shop_scaling
alt: A Diwali sweet shop comparing one superstar halwai with a giant kadhai against ten ordinary halwais at ten stoves.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves inside the busy back kitchen of a traditional Indian sweet shop decorated with marigold strings and small clay diyas for Diwali. LEFT panel: one single superstar halwai (large, confident, middle-aged, white vest, cloth headband, gold chain) stirs an enormous, comically oversized iron kadhai of bubbling syrup with a long paddle; the kadhai already nearly touches the ceiling, showing there is a limit to how big it can get, and a price tag-shaped bubble with stacked coins floats above him. RIGHT panel: ten ordinary halwais in plain vests stand in a neat row at ten small stoves, each cooking an identical small kadhai; between them a single shared recipe card hangs on a string and a shared sugar sack sits in the middle, with several hands reaching toward it at once, hinting at coordination trouble. In front of both kitchens, the shop counter is piled with boxes of kaju katli and a long queue of festive customers waits. Warm amber festive lighting, busy cheerful mood. Labels: "SCALE UP" at the top of the left panel, "SCALE OUT" at the top of the right panel.

key: Building a house vs living in it
name: ch01_house_maintainability
alt: A house shown at construction and then decades later with family members fixing pipes, repainting and adding a room.
scene: A wide, gently elevated illustration showing the same two-storey Indian house twice, left to right, like a timeline. On the far LEFT and small, the house under construction: bamboo scaffolding, a cement mixer, two masons laying bricks, a short bar marked by a tiny calendar icon to show a few months. On the RIGHT and much larger, the same house thirty years later, lived in and cut away like a dollhouse so we can see inside: an elderly father in a vest reaching easily into an open panel of neatly labelled pipes under the kitchen sink with a spanner; his grown-up daughter repainting a bedroom wall a fresh teal; a son and an electrician knocking out a light interior wall to add a nursery, with a baby cradle waiting nearby; a clear floor plan pinned to the fridge. A long horizontal timeline ribbon runs along the bottom of the image, short under the construction scene and stretching very long under the lived-in house, with small icons of a wrench, paint roller and brick along it. Warm late-afternoon light, homely, unhurried mood. Labels: "BUILD" under the construction scene, "MAINTAIN" along the long timeline, "EVOLVABILITY" beside the wall being knocked out.

key: A school report card. The relational
name: ch02_report_card_document
alt: A school office stapling a report card together from three separate registers, next to a single printed report card handed over in one go.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves set in an Indian school office with green walls, a ceiling fan and steel almirahs. LEFT panel: a harried school clerk (middle-aged woman, cotton saree, spectacles on a chain) sits at a wooden desk with three thick open registers spread in front of her, one with name columns, one with marks columns, one with attendance ticks; thin coloured lines connect the same roll number row across all three registers to a half-assembled report card in her hand, and she is reaching for a stapler while a waiting parent taps his watch. RIGHT panel: the same office, but a smiling clerk simply hands a single printed report card across the counter to a happy parent and his young son in school uniform; the card clearly shows a photo box, a marks table and an attendance section all on one sheet. A small speech-bubble shape near the right clerk shows a quick "one go" arrow from the cabinet to the parent. Soft morning light through a barred window, calm bureaucratic mood. Labels: "RELATIONAL" at the top of the left panel, "DOCUMENT" at the top of the right panel.

key: walk past the temple, second left
name: ch02_village_directions
alt: A traveller follows a hand-drawn route past a temple and a banyan tree, but the tree has been cut down and he stands confused.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a small Indian village. In the lower-left corner sits a rural bus stand with a tin shelter and a parked red bus. A bold dotted route line starts at the bus stand, runs past a small white temple with a saffron flag, and reaches a crossroads where a huge old banyan tree used to stand: now there is only a freshly cut stump with sawdust around it. At this crossroads a young traveller (early 20s, backpack, jeans, kurta) holds a crumpled paper of hand-drawn directions with sketch arrows, looking left and right with a puzzled face and a question mark above his head. Beyond, on the second lane to the left, a house with a bright blue gate is clearly visible but he cannot tell which lane to take. On the right edge of the scene, a railway station building with a separate path leads into the village from another direction, and the paper's route is no use from there. Village details: a cow, a hand pump, a tea shop. Midday sunlight, gentle comic mood. Labels: "ACCESS PATH" along the dotted route, "ROUTE BROKEN" next to the tree stump.

key: Election counting. At each booth
name: ch02_election_mapreduce
alt: Several polling booths sort ballots into piles in parallel, and slips flow to one table per candidate where they are added up.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view across a large Indian counting hall with high windows. On the LEFT third, three separate wooden booth tables side by side, each staffed by an election official (one older man in a white kurta and Nehru cap, one young woman in a saree with a lanyard, one middle-aged man with a moustache and spectacles) sorting paper ballots into small labelled piles marked only with candidate symbols (a star, a lamp, a flower), and writing tallies on little slips. Thin arrows of slips flow from all three booths toward the RIGHT third, where there are three result tables, one per candidate symbol, each receiving only the slips for that symbol; at each result table a counter adds them up on an old calculator. In the middle, the arrows cross over each other neatly like a sorting junction. One booth in the back has a recount happening calmly without disturbing the others. Ceiling fans, steel grille windows, cardboard ballot boxes with seals. Bright daylight, orderly, focused mood. Labels: "MAP" above the three booths, "GROUP BY KEY" over the crossing arrows in the middle, "REDUCE" above the three result tables.

key: A detective's evidence board
name: ch02_evidence_board_graph
alt: A detective studies an evidence board of photos and cards connected by coloured strings tagged with relationships.
scene: A warm, close-to-medium view of a cluttered detective's office at night. Most of the frame is filled by a large cork evidence board on the wall, covered with pinned photographs of anonymous people (simple silhouettes), index cards, a map of a city, a small picture of a house and a car. Coloured strings run between pins in every direction: red strings, blue strings and yellow strings, each string tagged with a tiny paper flag showing a small icon (a phone handset, a handshake, a rupee coin) rather than words. One card on the far edge is connected to a card on the opposite edge by a long string, showing any card can link to any other. In the lower right foreground, a detective (woman in her 40s, short hair, rolled-up shirt sleeves, cup of chai in one hand) is pinning a brand-new green string between two photos with her other hand, a spool of green thread on the desk beside a magnifying glass, files and a desk lamp. Moody yellow lamplight, focused investigative mood. Labels: "VERTICES" beside a cluster of photos, "EDGES" next to the bundle of strings, "NEW EDGE TYPE" by the green string.

key: where every booking change is written
name: ch03_append_only_register
alt: A railway clerk writes a new line at the bottom of a huge register instantly, but must scan every page to find the latest entry for one PNR.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same old railway reservation office with a wooden counter, a wall clock and a faded train timetable poster. The same clerk appears in both halves (middle-aged man, grey safari suit, spectacles, pen behind his ear). LEFT panel: he flips the giant register straight to the last page and writes one new line at the bottom with a quick confident stroke; a lightning-bolt icon beside him shows how fast it is. RIGHT panel: a passenger leans over the counter asking about a seat while the clerk, now sweating, runs his finger down page after page of a towering pile of register volumes from the very first page; small highlight marks show the same PNR appearing in several scattered lines, with the latest one buried somewhere in the middle of the stack. A tall queue of impatient passengers forms behind the enquirer. Afternoon light through barred windows, mildly comic mood. Visible text kept minimal: a small tag on a highlighted line reading "PNR 42". Labels: "APPEND: FAST" at the top of the left panel, "LOOKUP: SLOW" at the top of the right panel.

key: takes orders on a small whiteboard
name: ch03_chai_stall_lsm
alt: A chai stall owner writes orders on a sorted whiteboard and in a pocket diary, then copies a full board into a ledger page.
scene: A wide, eye-level illustration of a roadside chai stall, read left to right as a process. LEFT: the stall owner (40s, moustache, half-sleeve shirt, towel on shoulder) stands at the counter writing orders on a small whiteboard hanging beside him, where entries are neatly arranged in order by table number; at the same time, with his other hand, he scribbles the same order quickly into a small pocket diary in no order at all, with messy lines. Customers sit at numbered plastic tables in front. CENTRE: the whiteboard is now full; he copies it neatly onto a fresh ledger page, a curved arrow from the board into the ledger, then a duster wiping the board clean and a diary page being torn out and fluttering away. RIGHT: a shelf holding a growing stack of ledger pages, and a small inset at the far right where several pages are being merged by his assistant into one clean summary page with a paper clip. Steaming kettle, glass tumblers, biscuit jars, a sunny morning street behind. Warm, busy, orderly mood. Labels: "MEMTABLE" under the whiteboard, "WAL" under the pocket diary, "SSTABLE" under the ledger pages.

key: piles dirty plates in a tub
name: ch03_lsm_vs_btree_dishes
alt: Two restaurant kitchens: one piles dirty plates in a tub to wash at closing, the other washes every plate immediately.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, showing two side-by-side small Indian restaurant kitchens at night. LEFT panel: a fast-moving waiter (young man, black apron) drops dirty steel plates into a huge overflowing plastic tub without stopping, while diners in the doorway are served quickly; a wall clock reads late, and in the corner a dishwasher (older woman, sleeves rolled, hair tied up) faces a mountain of plates at closing time while a newly arrived order slip waits pinned on a spike, with a small hourglass icon beside it showing a sudden stall. RIGHT panel: a calmer kitchen where a cook-cum-washer (middle-aged man, white vest) rinses each plate at the sink immediately after use, a short steady stream of single plates going from table to sink to rack, the rack always neat; every order takes a little longer, shown by a small steady speedometer icon at a modest level, but there is no pile. Steam, steel utensils, hanging ladles, fluorescent kitchen light. Light-hearted, contrasting mood. Labels: "LSM" at the top of the left panel, "B-TREE" at the top of the right panel.

key: A school with 1,000 students and a
name: ch03_column_storage
alt: A principal reading the maths line from a mountain of report cards versus simply adding up one maths sheet.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both in a school principal's office with a wooden desk, a globe, and a framed map of India on the wall. The same principal appears in both halves (woman in her 50s, starched cotton saree, spectacles, grey bun). LEFT panel: she is buried behind a towering mountain of individual report cards, pulling them out one at a time and peering at just one highlighted line on each, with a tired expression; dozens of cards are scattered on the floor and a peon brings yet another bundle. RIGHT panel: the same desk is tidy; on it lie a few long sheets, each dedicated to one subject, arranged like separate tall columns, and she holds only one of them, a single long marks sheet, running a pen down it and smiling, a small calculator beside her showing the total. A small thin arrow points from that one sheet to a little average bubble. Soft daylight through a window with a neem tree outside, calm and clever mood. Labels: "ROW STORE" at the top of the left panel, "COLUMN STORE" at the top of the right panel, "MATHS" on the single sheet in her hand.

key: To send your recipe to your cousin
name: ch04_recipe_encoding
alt: A woman in her kitchen writes a full recipe for her cousin in Pune instead of a note saying see shelf 2; the cousin cooks from it in a different kitchen.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, two different Indian home kitchens. LEFT panel: a young woman (early 30s, salwar kameez, dupatta tied at the waist) stands in her own kitchen with open wooden shelves full of labelled steel jars; one jar on the second shelf has a sticky label pointing to another shelf, and a dotted pointer arrow loops from the jar to the shelf. She is writing on a sheet of paper on the counter, crossing out a short scribble and rewriting it in full, careful lines. A sealed envelope beside her is already addressed, and an arrow carries it out through a small window toward the right panel past a tiny train. RIGHT panel: in a completely different kitchen with a different shelf layout and a gas stove, her cousin (similar age, kurta, hair in a plait) reads the same sheet propped against a jar and measures two spoons of sugar into a pot, smiling. Visible text kept minimal: the crossed-out scribble reads "see shelf 2" and the rewritten line reads "2 spoons sugar". Warm morning light in both kitchens, homely mood. Labels: "ENCODE" at the top of the left panel, "DECODE" at the top of the right panel.

key: Exam hall seating. Avro is
name: ch04_exam_seating_tags
alt: Two exam halls: one seats students by name cards, the other by fixed seat numbers where an empty retired seat is roped off.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves showing a bright Indian college exam hall with rows of wooden desks, ceiling fans and a large wall clock. LEFT panel: each desk has a folded white name card standing on it (cards show only simple person silhouettes, no readable names); an invigilator (young woman, cotton kurta, lanyard) is cheerfully swapping two cards for a single fresh one as students rearrange themselves, showing seating follows the cards. RIGHT panel: each desk has a big painted seat number on its corner; one desk in the middle row is empty, roped off with a small red ribbon and a "retired" stamp-like tag, with an old answer sheet still lying on it; a late newcomer student (teenage boy, backpack) is being firmly redirected by a strict invigilator (older man, moustache, spectacles, holding a thick seat register) away from the retired desk to a brand-new desk at the end of the row. Visible text minimal: the retired desk shows the number "7". Calm morning light through tall windows, orderly mood. Labels: "BY NAME" at the top of the left panel, "BY TAG NUMBER" at the top of the right panel, "RETIRED" next to the roped-off desk.

key: pass the salt is a local call
name: ch04_courier_rpc
alt: Passing the salt across a dinner table compared with sending a courier across the city for money, with uncertainty about whether he arrived.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the left panel narrower than the right. LEFT panel: a cosy dining table where two young roommates (one in a T-shirt, one in a hoodie) sit across from each other; one simply hands the salt shaker to the other, a short solid arrow showing the action completed instantly in plain view. RIGHT panel: a wider city scene seen from slightly above. On the left edge, the same young man in the hoodie stands at his building gate handing a folded note to a courier rider on a motorbike. A long winding road crosses the city to a house on the far right where his cousin stands at the door with a wallet. Along the road, a dashed arrow goes to the house and a second dashed arrow returns, but the return arrow is broken in the middle by a big question mark and a small rain cloud, so we cannot tell where the courier got stuck. The young man looks worried, about to send a second courier who is already revving. Visible text kept minimal: the note shows "#17". Overcast light on the right, warm indoor light on the left. Labels: "LOCAL CALL" at the top of the left panel, "RPC" at the top of the right panel, "IDEMPOTENT" beside the note.

key: security desk taking courier parcels
name: ch04_security_desk_broker
alt: A courier drops a parcel at an apartment building's security desk and leaves, while the guard stores parcels and delivers copies of a notice to every flat.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of the entrance lobby of an Indian apartment building. On the LEFT, a delivery rider in a helmet and rain jacket drops a parcel onto the security desk and is already walking out toward his parked scooter, not waiting; a small arrow shows him leaving. In the CENTRE, the security guard (middle-aged man, khaki uniform, cap, moustache) sits at a wooden desk with a register and an intercom, and behind him a tall shelf of pigeonholes is filled with parcels of different sizes waiting for residents. On the RIGHT, a cut-away view of the building's floors: the guard's helper climbs the stairs to one flat whose door is closed, with a small circular retry arrow beside the door; on another floor, identical sheets of a notice are being slipped under every door at once, with thin arrows fanning out from one sheet to many doors. A resident in house clothes comes down later to collect her parcel from the shelf. Soft late-afternoon light, practical everyday mood. Labels: "BROKER" above the guard's desk, "BUFFER" by the parcel shelf, "FAN-OUT" beside the notices sliding under doors.

key: A wedding buffet with 10 counters
name: ch06_buffet_hot_spot
alt: A wedding buffet where a huge queue forms at the paneer counter while the other nine counters stand idle.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of a grand Indian wedding lawn at night under strings of fairy lights and a decorated shamiana. Ten buffet counters stand in a long gentle arc, each with a steel chafing dish and a cook in a white chef's coat and cap. At one counter near the centre, the paneer counter, a huge snaking queue of guests in festive clothes (women in bright sarees and lehengas, men in kurtas and sherwanis, children tugging at parents) crowds forward, plates held out; the cook there is sweating and serving frantically with a ladle. At the other nine counters, the cooks lean idly on the tables, one yawns, one checks his phone, one chats with another; their dishes steam untouched. A thick glowing heat-shimmer around the busy counter emphasises the crowding. In the lower-right corner, a small inset circle shows the opposite trick: a single guest walking a dotted path past all ten counters looking for gulab jamun hidden at a random one. Warm golden light, festive but slightly comic mood. Labels: "HOT SPOT" above the crowded paneer counter, "IDLE NODES" above the quiet counters.

key: A bank with branches in Pune and Nashik
name: ch06_bank_local_index
alt: A bank officer phones two branches, each holding its own register, and waits for the slowest branch manager to answer.
scene: A wide illustration organised as a triangle. At the top centre, at a head-office desk, a bank officer (woman in her 30s, formal kurta, ID card, headset) holds two old telephone receivers, one to each ear, waiting with a drumming finger and a slight frown; a notepad in front of her shows a small partial tally. At the bottom LEFT, inside a small bank branch with a teak counter and a signboard showing only a simple city skyline icon, a quick, cheerful branch manager (young man, tie, rolled sleeves) has already found the answer in his thin surname register and is speaking into the phone. At the bottom RIGHT, another branch where an older, slower manager (bald, spectacles, sweater vest) is buried in a cupboard full of dusty registers, still searching page by page, with a tiny clock icon over his head. Phone cords link both branches up to the officer like two arrows, the right one dotted to show the wait. A customer at the left branch is opening an account that only touches that branch's register. Soft office light, mildly comic, waiting mood. Labels: "LOCAL INDEX" by each branch register, "SCATTER/GATHER" near the officer.

key: packs tiffins into 1,000 crates
name: ch06_dabbawala_fixed_partitions
alt: Dabbawalas hand whole numbered crates of tiffins to a newly joined rider without re-sorting any tiffins.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of a busy Mumbai street outside a suburban railway station at late morning. Many identical wooden crates, each holding rows of round steel tiffins and each with a large painted number on its side, are lined up. Four dabbawalas in white kurta-pyjamas and white Gandhi caps stand with their bicycles and one bigger cargo tricycle; the rider with the larger tricycle carries more crates than the others. In the centre, a brand-new young rider (late teens, eager smile, crisp white cap) has just arrived with an empty bike, and each existing rider is handing him one or two whole crates; curved arrows from three riders converge on the newcomer. No one is opening crates or moving individual tiffins. One crate in transit is still roped to its old rider's bike while the hand-over happens. A painted code on one tiffin lid reads only "417", and the crate holding it reads "417" too, showing the tiffin's crate never changes. Busy station arches, a local train and pigeons in the background. Bright, energetic mood. Labels: "FIXED PARTITIONS" above the row of crates, "NEW NODE" above the newcomer, "REBALANCE" along the converging arrows.

key: Finding a person in a big office
name: ch06_office_request_routing
alt: Three ways to find a colleague in an office: ask any employee, ask reception with a seating chart, or carry your own chart.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated cut-away view of a modern Indian open-plan office floor, with a visitor shown three times along a left-to-right path. LEFT: the visitor (young man, formal shirt, visitor badge, folder under his arm) asks a random employee at a desk, who stands up and walks him toward the correct desk, dotted footsteps showing the extra hop. CENTRE: a reception desk where a receptionist (woman, neat bun, blazer) points at a large wall-mounted seating chart with coloured desk blocks and directs the visitor with an arrow straight to the right desk. RIGHT: the same visitor walking confidently straight to the right desk reading a small folded copy of the seating chart in his own hand. In the background, near a pantry, two employees chat over chai with tiny speech bubbles containing a simple arrow icon to a different floor, showing gossip spreading desk changes. At the far right, the target colleague (woman, headphones, laptop) waves. Bright daytime office light, plants, glass partitions, friendly mood. Labels: "ANY NODE" above the left scene, "ROUTING TIER" above reception, "SMART CLIENT" above the right scene.

key: Two cashiers at a chai stall share
name: ch07_chai_lost_update
alt: Two chai stall cashiers both read 42 on a shared whiteboard, each sell a cup, and both write 43, losing one count.
scene: A wide, eye-level illustration of a busy chai stall with a single small whiteboard hanging in the middle of the counter. Two cashiers stand on either side of it: on the left a young man in a red checked shirt, on the right a young woman in a yellow kurta with a dupatta. The scene is shown as a short sequence within one frame using faint ghost poses. First, both glance at the board at the same moment, thought bubbles above each of them showing the same number. Then each hands a glass of chai to a different customer at their side of the counter. Finally both reach up with markers at the same time, one wiping with a cloth, and the board shows a single number written twice, overlapping and slightly smudged. Below the counter, two customers clearly hold two separate glasses of chai, but only one tick is visible on the board. A steaming kettle and biscuit jars in the background, morning street behind. Visible text kept minimal: the thought bubbles both read "42" and the board reads "43". Bright, slightly comic mood. Labels: "LOST UPDATE" at the top centre above the whiteboard, "RACE" small between the two cashiers.

key: Counting the crowd at a moving train
name: ch07_platform_snapshot
alt: A railway official walking past coaches counting passengers who hop between coaches, versus counting from one photograph of the whole platform.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both showing a crowded Indian railway platform beside a long train with twelve coaches. LEFT panel: a railway official (middle- aged man, white uniform, cap, clicker counter in hand) walks along the coaches from the first toward the last, frowning; behind him, passengers with bags hop from one coach door to the next, small curved arrows showing some being counted twice and others slipping past uncounted, and a tea vendor weaves between them. RIGHT panel: a young woman railway staffer (blue uniform, ponytail) stands on a footbridge above the platform holding up a camera and capturing the entire platform in one frame; a printed photograph floats in the corner as an inset, where the people are frozen in place and she is calmly ticking them off with a pen. The moving crowd below the footbridge continues to blur slightly, but the photo stays still. Overhead station roof, hanging signboards with only simple coach number shapes, mid-morning light. Busy left side, calm right side. Labels: "NO SNAPSHOT" at the top of the left panel, "SNAPSHOT ISOLATION" at the top of the right panel.

key: Two security guards at a society gate
name: ch07_guards_write_skew
alt: Two security guards at a gate each see the other on duty and both step out for chai at the same moment, leaving the gate empty.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, showing two moments at the same housing society gate with an iron gate, a small guard cabin and a register on a stool. LEFT panel, the moment of decision: two guards in khaki uniforms and caps stand at opposite ends of the gate, one tall and thin, one short and round. Each glances sideways at the other, and each has a thought bubble showing a tiny picture of the other guard still standing at the gate, alongside a steaming cup of chai, meaning he is here so I can go. RIGHT panel, a minute later: both guards are walking away in opposite directions toward two different tea stalls across the road, each relaxed and holding a cup, while the gate between them stands completely empty and slightly open; a stray dog wanders in and a delivery van pulls up with no one to stop it. A small wall sign near the cabin shows a simple icon of one guard figure with a "1" next to it. Afternoon sunlight, quiet residential street with trees, gently comic mood. Labels: "EACH CHECKS" at the top of the left panel, "WRITE SKEW" at the top of the right panel, "RULE BROKEN" beside the empty gate.

key: narrow one-lane bridge from opposite
name: ch07_bridge_deadlock
alt: Two cars face each other on a narrow one-lane bridge, each waiting, until a traffic policeman orders one to reverse.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a narrow old stone one-lane bridge over a river in hilly Indian countryside. In the middle of the bridge two cars face each other bumper to bumper: on the left a small white hatchback, on the right a blue old-style sedan. Each driver leans out of the window gesturing at the other to reverse, with an annoyed expression and small circling arrows above both cars showing an endless wait loop. Queues of vehicles stretch behind each car: an auto-rickshaw, a goods truck, a motorbike, a bullock cart. In the foreground on the right bank, a traffic policeman (khaki uniform, white sleeves, white cap, whistle in mouth) raises one white-gloved hand firmly toward the blue sedan, and a large bold reverse arrow shows the sedan backing off the bridge entirely so the hatchback can pass, the sedan's driver looking resigned. River flowing below, green hills, a small temple on a hilltop. Late morning light, comic but tense mood. Labels: "DEADLOCK" above the two cars, "DETECTOR" next to the policeman, "ABORT AND RETRY" along the reverse arrow.

key: message to the electrician
name: ch08_electrician_no_reply
alt: A homeowner stares at a message with one grey tick while inset bubbles show the many possible reasons the electrician has not replied.
scene: A wide illustration with a central figure and four surrounding inset bubbles. In the centre, in a living room with a flickering ceiling light and a dead switchboard, a homeowner (man in his 30s, vest and pyjamas, slightly anxious) holds up his phone; the screen shows a single chat bubble with only one grey tick. Around him, connected by dotted lines that all end in question marks, are four possibilities as round inset bubbles: top-left, the electrician's phone lying switched off on a charger; top-right, the electrician in a basement typing a reply that is stuck with a red no-signal icon; bottom-left, the electrician up a tall ladder with both hands busy fixing wires; bottom-right, the electrician already on his scooter riding toward the house with a toolbox. From the centre figure's point of view all four look identical: the dotted lines are the same grey. In a small corner at the far right, a second electrician arrives at the door holding a toolbox while the first one also pulls up outside, both looking confused. Evening light, mildly comic, uncertain mood. Visible text kept minimal. Labels: "NO RESPONSE" above the phone, "TIMEOUT" near the two electricians at the door.

key: The wall clock in your kitchen vs the
name: ch08_wall_clock_vs_stopwatch
alt: A wall clock being turned back while an egg boils, compared with a phone stopwatch that keeps counting steadily.
scene: A wide, eye-level illustration of a homely Indian kitchen, split visually into left and right halves without a hard line. LEFT: a round wall clock above the gas stove, and a mischievous teenage boy standing on a stool turning its hands backwards with his finger, a curved backwards arrow showing the jump; on the stove, a small steel pot with an egg boiling in it. A young woman cook (20s, salwar kameez, hair tied) looks up at the clock confused, holding a notepad where a calculation ends in a minus sign. RIGHT: on the counter, her phone stands on a stand showing a large stopwatch face with a steadily advancing sweep and a small forward arrow, unaffected by the boy. A thin dotted line from the egg pot leads to the phone, showing that she should time the egg with this instead. A small inset bubble at the far right shows a friend's phone with its own stopwatch reading something different, with an equals sign crossed out between the two phones. Warm morning light, steam rising, playful mood. Labels: "TIME-OF-DAY CLOCK" under the wall clock, "MONOTONIC CLOCK" under the phone stopwatch.

key: dozes off on his chair for 20 minutes
name: ch08_guard_process_pause
alt: A security guard dozes off on his chair past his shift end, wakes up and confidently stops a visitor whom the new guard has already let in.
scene: A wide illustration read left to right as three moments at the same office building entrance with a glass door, a wall clock and a guard cabin. LEFT: the first guard (middle-aged, khaki uniform, cap, moustache) checks a duty roster clipboard, relaxed; the wall clock shows a minute before ten. CENTRE: the same guard slumped asleep on a plastic chair, cap tilted over his eyes, a few "Z" shapes floating up, while the wall clock behind him has jumped forward; a second guard (younger, same uniform, alert) has arrived and taken over the cabin, and is waving a visitor (woman with a laptop bag and ID card) in through the door. RIGHT: the first guard has just woken up, jumped to his feet and is confidently holding up his hand to stop the same visitor, who is already inside, while the second guard is gesturing her forward; the visitor looks torn between them. Small conflict sparks between the two guards. The clock now shows nearly twenty past ten. Morning light through glass, comic, confused mood. Labels: "PROCESS PAUSE" above the sleeping guard, "STALE LEASE" above the woken guard, "CONFLICT" between the two guards.

key: A housing society committee of 5
name: ch08_committee_quorum
alt: A society committee of five votes three to two to remove the secretary, who protests but hands over the keys.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of a housing society meeting held in a community hall with plastic chairs, a ceiling fan and a long table draped with a cloth. Five committee members sit or stand around the table. On the right, three of them (an elderly woman in a cotton saree, a young man in a T-shirt and a middle-aged man in a kurta) raise their hands together in a clear vote, a soft glowing outline grouping the three. On the left, two members keep their hands down. At the head of the table, the outgoing secretary (portly man in his 50s, spectacles, waistcoat) stands with one finger raised, mouth open mid-protest, a speech bubble showing only an exclamation mark, while with his other hand he reluctantly holds out a bunch of keys toward the newly chosen secretary (woman in her 40s, confident, holding a file). A curved arrow shows the keys moving from him to her. On the wall behind them, a simple tally on a small blackboard shows three marks on one side and two on the other. Evening tube-light glow, lively civic mood. Labels: "QUORUM" above the three raised hands, "MAJORITY DECIDES" at the top centre.

key: India vs Pakistan, last ball
name: ch09_scoreboard_linearizability
alt: A friend shouts that India won while another person's phone, refreshed afterwards, still shows the old score.
scene: A wide, eye-level illustration of a crowded living room during a tense cricket match, the TV off to the side showing only a blurred stadium. On the LEFT, an excited young man (blue cricket jersey, painted tricolour cheeks) jumps up from the sofa with both arms raised, phone held high in one hand, shouting with a big speech bubble showing a trophy and fireworks icon. On the RIGHT, his friend (glasses, hoodie, chips packet on his lap) looks down at his own phone right after refreshing it, with a small circular refresh arrow above the screen, and the screen still shows the old tense score; his face is a mixture of confusion and suspicion. A dotted timeline arrow runs along the bottom of the scene from left to right, with a small dot labelled by a shout icon first and a later dot with a refresh icon, showing the refresh clearly happened after the shout. Visible text kept minimal: the right-hand phone screen reads "need 2 off 1". Snacks, a cushion flying, an elderly grandmother watching curiously from the doorway. Warm evening lamp light, energetic, comic mood. Labels: "STALE READ" above the friend's phone, "LINEARIZABLE?" at the top centre.

key: core server in Mumbai and a branch in
name: ch09_bank_partition_cap
alt: A Guwahati bank branch cut off from Mumbai must choose between refusing deposits or writing them in a paper register.
scene: A wide composition with a map-like background of India in soft tones. At the far LEFT, a tall bank headquarters building with a server room glowing inside, set by the sea. At the far RIGHT, near hills and tea gardens, a small branch office. Between them a long cable line runs across the map and is clearly snapped in the middle, with a broken plug and a small spark. The branch is shown as a split view, divided by a thin vertical line down its middle. Left half of the branch: a clerk (young man, tie, glasses) behind the counter holds up a small sign showing a closed-shutter icon, and a customer with a cash envelope turns away disappointed. Right half: another clerk (woman in a cotton saree) cheerfully accepts the deposit and writes it into a thick paper register, with a small sync arrow waiting by the register and a faint ghost image of a second person withdrawing the same money at a far window. Soft daylight, thoughtful mood. Labels: "PARTITION" over the snapped cable, "CONSISTENT" above the refusing clerk, "AVAILABLE" above the clerk writing in the register.

key: A Hindu wedding needs both families
name: ch09_wedding_two_phase_commit
alt: A pandit at a wedding mandap first asks both families if they are ready, then proceeds once both say yes.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both showing a decorated wedding mandap with marigold garlands, banana leaves, a small sacred fire and brass lamps. LEFT panel: the pandit (elderly, bald with a small tuft, white dhoti, sacred thread, rudraksha beads) stands between two family groups, turning first to the bride's side and then to the groom's side with an open hand, two curved dotted arrows going out to each family with a small question-mark bubble. The bride's family (her parents in silk saree and kurta, an aunt) and the groom's family (his parents and an uncle in a turban) each send back a small solid arrow with a tick bubble. RIGHT panel: the pandit now raises both hands and announces; the bride (red lehenga, jewellery) and groom (cream sherwani, safa) begin walking around the fire, joined by the tied cloth, and flower petals fly while both families cheer. Warm golden firelight, joyful ceremonial mood. Labels: "PREPARE" at the top of the left panel, "COMMIT" at the top of the right panel, "COORDINATOR" under the pandit in the left panel.

key: A gram sabha choosing one candidate
name: ch09_gram_sabha_consensus
alt: A village assembly under a banyan tree reaches a majority decision on one sarpanch candidate, and everyone leaves knowing the same name.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of a village gram sabha meeting held under a huge banyan tree in a dusty village square. On a low raised platform sit the presiding officers at a simple table with a register. Three nominated candidates stand to one side, each wearing a garland and holding a placard with only a simple symbol (a lamp, a wheel, a tree), no names. In front, a large crowd of villagers sits on durries: farmers in turbans and dhotis, women in colourful sarees, elderly men with walking sticks, young people. Most raise their hands for the lamp candidate, and a soft glowing outline groups this clear majority. On the edge, a couple of empty spots with a small stretcher-like cot show that a few villagers are ill and absent, yet the meeting goes on. On the right, the crowd leaves along a path, and every head has a small identical thought bubble showing the same lamp symbol. A small official notice board by the tree shows only the lamp symbol pinned up. Late afternoon light, dignified, communal mood. Labels: "QUORUM" above the raised hands, "AGREEMENT" above the leaving crowd's identical bubbles.

key: only sorts them at the station by colour
name: ch10_dabbawala_pipeline
alt: A chain of dabbawalas each doing one job: collecting tiffins, sorting by colour code, carrying on the train and delivering to offices.
scene: A wide panoramic illustration read left to right like a relay, with four stages separated by gentle gaps. STAGE 1, far left: a residential lane where a dabbawala in white kurta-pyjama and white Gandhi cap collects round steel tiffins from a housewife at her door and hangs them on his bicycle. STAGE 2: a railway platform where a second dabbawala sits on the ground sorting tiffins into wooden crates by the coloured painted codes on their lids, tiffins in neat colour groups. STAGE 3: a crowded Mumbai local train with a third dabbawala standing in the luggage compartment holding a crate steady. STAGE 4, far right: a busy office lobby where a fourth dabbawala hands a tiffin to a smiling office worker in a tie. Bold arrows connect each stage to the next. Between stage 2 and stage 3 a newly added fifth dabbawala with a small clipboard is slotted in, doing a quick quality check, with a little plus sign above him. None of the dabbawalas looks at a map. Bright late-morning light, energetic, harmonious mood. Labels: "ONE JOB EACH" at the top centre, "PIPE" along the arrows, "NEW STEP" above the quality checker.

key: An election counting centre. Mappers
name: ch10_counting_centre_mapreduce
alt: Clerks open ballot boxes and write slips, trays route slips by candidate, and one counter per tray counts them.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of a large election counting centre in a school hall with high windows and ceiling fans. LEFT third: a row of clerks (a young woman in a saree, an older man in a white kurta, a young man in a shirt with a lanyard) sit at desks breaking the seals on metal ballot boxes and writing one small paper slip per vote, each slip showing only a candidate symbol (a lamp, a flower, a wheel). CENTRE third: a clever system of slanted wooden chutes and trays carries every slip toward the tray for its symbol, slips sliding down neatly sorted, with arrows crossing from all clerks into the trays. RIGHT third: three counters, one sitting at each tray, quietly counting their own stack with tally marks; each one only looks at their own tray. In the background, a late clerk still opening a final ballot box, with the counters glancing toward him, waiting. Police guard at the door, cardboard boxes, a wall clock. Bright daylight, orderly, focused mood. Labels: "MAPPERS" above the clerks, "SHUFFLE" over the chutes, "REDUCERS" above the counters.

key: Fan mail at a TV channel. Normally
name: ch10_fan_mail_skew
alt: One staffer at a TV channel is buried under a superstar's fan mail while colleagues are idle, then the letters are spread across everyone.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both inside the open-plan back office of a TV channel with posters of simple show icons on the wall. LEFT panel: one young staffer (woman, cardigan, spectacles) is almost completely buried under a towering mountain of envelopes on her desk, only her hands and the top of her head visible; mail sacks keep arriving; her colleagues at neighbouring desks sit with tiny piles, sipping tea and checking the wall clock, waiting for her before they can go home. RIGHT panel: the same office, now the mountain of envelopes is split into equal small piles and spread across every desk by a manager with arrows fanning out; each staffer has a small stack and a photocopy of the same standard reply card on their desk; a supervisor at the end table adds up small total slips from everyone into one final number. A small star icon marks the superstar's letters in both panels. Office tube-light, mildly comic then relieved mood. Labels: "SKEW" at the top of the left panel, "SPREAD THE HOT KEY" at the top of the right panel.

key: class-monitor network passing a message
name: ch10_class_monitor_pregel
alt: School class monitors read notes in their pigeonholes, update their best route and pass notes on, while a bell marks each round.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated cut-away view of a school corridor with several classrooms side by side. In each classroom doorway stands a class monitor (schoolchildren in uniform, a monitor badge on each), each with a small wooden pigeonhole box mounted beside their door. Thin string-like lines connect neighbouring classrooms like a network map. One monitor (girl with two plaits) reads a folded note from her pigeonhole and corrects a route sketch on her slate with a shorter line; another (boy with spectacles) slips folded notes into his neighbours' pigeonholes, arrows showing them travelling along the strings; one monitor whose pigeonhole is empty just sits on a bench waiting. At the end of the corridor, a peon in a khaki uniform rings a large brass school bell, with sound waves rippling over all classrooms, and a slow monitor at the far end is still writing while others wait for him. A small inset at the top right shows a simple map with a dotted route to an exam centre building. Bright daytime light, orderly, playful mood. Labels: "SUPERSTEP" above the classrooms, "BARRIER" under the ringing bell.

key: The chaiwala makes 3 cups a minute
name: ch11_chai_backpressure
alt: A chai stall at rush hour shown three ways: ignoring extra customers, letting order slips pile up, and stopping token sales so customers wait.
scene: A wide illustration of the same busy roadside chai stall at evening rush hour shown as three side-by-side panels divided by thin vertical lines. In each panel the same chaiwala (middle-aged, moustache, checked shirt, towel on shoulder) pours tea from a kettle at a steady pace. LEFT panel: a crowd of office-goers shouts orders, and a few customers at the back are turned away with a crossed hand gesture, walking off annoyed, empty-handed. CENTRE panel: every order is written on a little paper slip and stuck on the counter, and the pile of slips has grown so tall that it spills over the edge and flutters onto the road. RIGHT panel: a young cashier at a small token table has placed a small closed sign shaped like a hand on the token box, and customers wait calmly in an orderly line outside a rope, while the chaiwala serves at his own pace and cups are exactly matched to tokens. Steam rising, sodium street lights, scooters parked nearby, busy commuter mood. Labels: "DROP" at the top of the left panel, "BUFFER" at the top of the centre panel, "BACKPRESSURE" at the top of the right panel.

key: a tear-off token roll at a sweet shop
name: ch11_token_roll_vs_bill_book
alt: A sweet shop's tear-off token roll whose tokens disappear once given, beside a carbon-copy bill book an accountant re-reads later.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both inside the same traditional Indian sweet shop with glass display cases full of laddoos, jalebis and barfis. LEFT panel, daytime: a shop boy (teenager, white vest, cap) tears tokens off a red paper roll mounted on the counter and hands each one to a customer; the customers walk away and the tokens leave with them, a few torn stubs fluttering and fading into nothing, with a small dotted arrow ending in an empty space. RIGHT panel, evening, the shop closed with the shutter half down: an elderly accountant (white kurta, spectacles on his nose, pencil behind his ear) sits cross-legged on a gaddi with a thick bill book on a low desk, its carbon copies all still bound inside, flipping back to the first page; a curved rewind arrow loops from the last page back to the first, and a small adding machine beside him prints a long tape. A second younger accountant waits with her own notepad to read the same book later. Warm tube-light glow, calm mood. Labels: "MESSAGE QUEUE" at the top of the left panel, "LOG" at the top of the right panel, "REPLAY" beside the rewind arrow.

key: Your bank passbook lists every deposit
name: ch11_passbook_event_sourcing
alt: An open bank passbook listing every deposit and withdrawal, with the balance derived at the bottom of each page.
scene: A wide, warm illustration inside a small Indian bank branch. In the foreground on a wooden counter lies a large open passbook, shown big and clear, with rows of entries on each page: small green up-arrows for deposits and small red down-arrows for withdrawals, without readable text. At the bottom of each page a highlighted box holds the running balance, and thin brackets on the side show that the balance is built from all the arrows above it. On the left, a customer (retired man, white shirt, cap, cloth bag) points at the page with satisfaction. Behind the counter, a teller (young woman, formal kurta, ID card) is feeding the passbook into a passbook-printing machine that adds a new line. On the right side, a small inset thought bubble from a confused trainee clerk shows him trying to erase all lines except the last salary line, with a big red cross over that idea. In the background, shelves of old archived passbooks tied with string. Afternoon light through a barred window, calm, trustworthy mood. Labels: "EVENTS" along the list of entries, "SNAPSHOT" beside the page-bottom balance box.

key: collecting exam answer sheets at 1:00 pm
name: ch11_late_answer_sheet
alt: A teacher has sealed a bundle of answer sheets when a late student runs in from the sick room with one more sheet.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of a school exam corridor and classroom just after an exam. In the centre, a teacher (woman in her 40s, cotton saree, spectacles on a chain) stands at a desk having just tied and sealed a thick bundle of answer sheets with string and red sealing wax; a wall clock above her shows just past one. Through the doorway, a nearly empty corridor. Running in from the far end of the corridor marked by a small red-cross sign over a sick-room door, a breathless student (teenage boy, school uniform, bandage on his forehead) waves one answer sheet. The teacher has two thought bubbles: one shows her writing a small tally mark in a register, the other shows her cutting the string to reopen the bundle and sending a corrected count on a slip to the office. At the building's entrance, a peon in khaki stands announcing with a raised hand that everyone has left, while behind him a student peeks out from behind a library door. Afternoon light, gently comic mood. Labels: "LATE EVENT" above the running student, "WATERMARK" beside the peon.
